children: CBOT grains are pulling back as traders attempt to factor in the risk potential for headlines out of the President Trump's summit with Chinese president Xi in Washington. But some traders think that the meeting is more likely to produce news supportive for higher prices. "Trump has been playing nice with Asian leaders as of late, even posting a series of pics with Kim Jong Un and Xi in the past couple months," says Jason Snow of Futures International. "So I'd expect more friendly postings once again." Most-active corn futures fall 1.3%, soybeans are down 0.8%, and wheat is off 1.4%. (kirk.maltais@wsj.com)
